primitives.name: Missed Tackles Forced
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Missed tackles forced (MTF)** — stat box on Carry Charts (Walker 15, Gibbs 12).
primitives.assumptions: Player-level tracking data available for tackle events; MTF is computed as the difference between attempted and successful tackles in a given context.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Per-play or per-player aggregate over a season or window.

layer2.mapping: Derived from tracking data on tackle success/failure, used in GSE for evaluating defensive efficiency and player impact in run defense.
layer2.telemetry: Number of missed tackles per player or team, verified via nflverse or FTN proxy datasets.

primitives.name: Rushing Yards Over Expected
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Rushing yards over expected (RYOE)** — stat box on Carry Charts (+101 Walker, +21 Gibbs).
primitives.assumptions: Expected rushing yards are modeled using historical averages or regression-based projections; RYOE is the deviation from that expectation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Per-play or cumulative over a season or window.

layer2.mapping: Computed as actual rushing yards minus expected yards, used in GSE to assess offensive efficiency and running back performance.
layer2.telemetry: Cumulative yards above expected, validated against nflverse or FTN tracking models.

primitives.name: Completion Percentage Over Expected
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Completion percentage over expected (CPOE)** — stat box on Pass Charts (+16.7% Purdy, +10.9% Dart, 55.3% Allen).
primitives.assumptions: Expected completion percentage is estimated using historical data and situational factors; CPOE is the difference between observed and expected values.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Per-game or per-quarter, aggregated over a season.

layer2.mapping: Computed as actual completion percentage minus expected, used in GSE to evaluate quarterback performance and pass efficiency.
layer2.telemetry: Percentage point difference from expected, validated via public tracking models.

The failure mode arises when tracking data lacks granularity or when baseline models are misaligned with current game dynamics. Dualities emerge in how metrics like RYOE and CPOE reflect opposing sides of offensive performance—defensive pressure and offensive execution respectively. These operators are embedded in a Bayesian framework within GSI, where prior distributions are informed by historical tracking proxies.
